# Proposed architecture decision

**Status: Proposed — project acceptance required.**

Engine 0.8.0; catalog 0.5.0; services 0.8.0; analysis 0.2.0.
Input SHA-256: c8964c0fb813d6e0be335803dffe6ec33754d77ca3121e5933e2aa41daf61f09.

## Original result

PROVISIONAL STACK — unresolved critical constraints require review before production\. modular\_monolith recommendation selected from 270 complete compatible plans; month\-12 infrastructure planning band USD 366\.9–614\.06/month\.
Result: ok_with_warnings.

- frontend: Angular — Covers requested targets web with spa rendering\. Team languages: go, typescript\. Selected after supporting\-service compatibility and whole\-plan infrastructure cost scoring\. Explicit critical warnings identify provisional data\-flow/control exceptions\.
- backend: Express — Provides a node application runtime for the realtime\_collab profile\. Language familiarity and delivery complexity were compared across compatible whole plans\. Selected after supporting\-service compatibility and whole\-plan infrastructure cost scoring\. Explicit critical warnings identify provisional data\-flow/control exceptions\.
- database: Supabase Pro PostgreSQL — relational persistence via Supabase Pro, one regional PostgreSQL project\.  Database drivers and host deployment were checked as a combination\. Selected after supporting\-service compatibility and whole\-plan infrastructure cost scoring\. Explicit critical warnings identify provisional data\-flow/control exceptions\.
- hosting: Fly\.io regional Machines — Matches managed\_cloud with provider fly; reviewed primary compute region iad\. Required runtimes and separate database deployment were checked\. Selected after supporting\-service compatibility and whole\-plan infrastructure cost scoring\. Explicit critical warnings identify provisional data\-flow/control exceptions\.

Monthly infrastructure/operations band (activity fees additional): USD 366.9–614.06.

## Complete alternatives

- modular\_monolith\|angular\|express\|supabase\-pg\|fly\|iad; score 89; USD 366.9–614.06; selected.
- modular\_monolith\|angular\|fastify\|supabase\-pg\|fly\|iad; score 89; USD 366.9–614.06; alternative.
- modular\_monolith\|angular\|go\-http\|supabase\-pg\|fly\|iad; score 89; USD 366.9–614.06; alternative.

## Preference stability

Original winner retained in 25/25 tested settings; 1 observed winners. Counts are not confidence probabilities.

## Cost assumptions

- Horizon: expected month\-12 footprint; 730 hours/month\. No tax, development/on\-call labor, domain registration or new on\-prem hardware procurement is included\.
- Peak concurrency supplied: 5000; not equated directly with requests/second\.
- RPS absent: authored daily\-active fraction 0\.2 of registered month\-12 users, floored at supplied peak concurrency \(10000 active/day\); 50 requests/active user/day gives 5\.787 average RPS\. Neither fraction nor request rate is measured; explicit RPS overrides both\. Peak capacity is separate\.
- Data volume 200 GB supplied; egress 500 GB/month assumed at 0\.01 GB per year\-12 user, minimum 1 GB; backup retention 1 months assumed\.
- Fly: 12 always\-on shared\-CPU/2GiB reference Machines, no first\-month/free\-credit assumption\. Reference sizing 50 RPS or 500 realtime/1000 other peak users per allocation is authored and unvalidated\. No India region mapping; no guarantee of p95/HA\. Select a dedicated class after CPU testing if necessary\.
- Supabase Pro is one specific regional project, not a self\-hosted PostgreSQL alias\. Micro/Medium connection pools and CPU/RAM require validation; limit application pools and prefer transaction pooling\. Default DB backups are daily/seven days \(provider assumption overriding generic one\-month backup assumption for DB only\); no explicit month\-retention extension is accepted by this profile\. Object backup is separately charged\. No HIPAA Pro eligibility or contractual SLA is claimed\.
- Payment assumptions: 0–1000 transactions/month, average USD 50; missing count assumes up to 2% of year\-12 users and missing ticket assumes USD 50\. Percentage/fixed rates are declared envelopes, not verified merchant pricing\. Payout, FX, tax, refunds and chargebacks require separate quotes\.
- Headline estimate and budget fit cover infrastructure/operations only\. Payment and SMS activity fees are separately itemized scenarios and excluded from this total; missing volumes are assumptions, not measured expenditure\.
- 100 GB file storage included once, then USD \.0213/GB\.
- 250 GB uncached allowance once; no additional cached allowance assumed\. Includes database\-to\-application plus direct client traffic within authored envelope; actual routing must be measured\.
- 500 included peak connections; USD 10 per additional 1000\-connection package\.
- 8 GB included once; application data distribution between DB/files unknown, database uses 50–100% total data\.
- All month\-12 users conservatively treated as monthly active auth users; 100k included once\.
- Always\-on shared\-cpu\-2x/2GiB reference Machines USD 13\.39 per 30 days in US; 730\-hour month\. Frankfurt upper adds an authored 50% regional allowance, not an exact quote\. Shared CPU is not dedicated CPU\.
- Assumed fee fraction, not quoted pricing; merchant country, card mix and extras vary\.
- Assumed per\-transaction USD fee envelope, not a tariff quote\.
- Authored 1–2 realtime messages per API request, 5M included then USD 2\.50/M\. Broadcast fan\-out may cost more; measure it\.
- Authored extra operations/retention headroom, not unlimited native log storage\.
- Authored hosted build\-minute allowance, assuming included quota at the lower bound\. Paid runners/minutes/artifacts require a repository\-specific quote and spending cap\.
- Authored minimum USD 5/month regional logs/metrics archive allowance, separate from included runtime logs\.
- Authored separately stored file backup allowance at USD \.05/GB\-month; provider/database backup does not protect object bytes\. Destination geography, transfer and restore implementation require review\.
- One USD 25 Pro organization/project; charge 730 hours of Micro \(\.01344/h\), or Medium \(\.0822/h\) when peak >=1000, minus one USD 10 compute credit\. Tier threshold is an unvalidated capacity hypothesis\.
- US/EU public outbound; cross\-provider database traffic is charged separately by its service\. Private inter\-region traffic and dedicated addresses need deployment\-specific quote\.

## Blockers, validation and owner actions

- critical: This paid managed tier is a planning proposal, not validated capacity or an availability SLA\. Validate pool limits, concurrent clients, CPU/memory, backup restore and the requested p95/availability before deployment; no automatic HA replicas are assumed\.
- warning: 99\.9% is a target, not a product guarantee\. The cost model provisions redundancy assumptions; service terms, failover and workload behavior still require verification\.
- warning: The output proposes technical control designs only\. It does not certify compliance, establish legal applicability, execute contracts, or replace an audit\. Implement controls and obtain scope\-specific review\.
- warning: Social provider selection and privacy/transfer terms need explicit review; Keycloak is only the local broker\.
- warning: No measured evidence establishes the 100 ms p95 target; load\-test the complete client/network/data path\.
- warning: Planning bands combine published reference rates and explicitly authored allowances; they are not regional provider quotes or measured workload capacity\. Validate sizing, merchant/SMS eligibility, storage, requests and current tariffs before purchase\.
- scale\.peak\_concurrent\_users, requirements\.availability: Review the scoped catalog evidence, workload and configuration; resolve the condition and rerun the unchanged input\.

## Evidence register

- core:angular: [Angular deployment](https://angular.dev/tools/cli/deployment); checked 2026\-11\-13; Web asset deployment
- core:express\-db: [Express database integration](https://expressjs.com/en/guide/database-integration/); checked 2026\-11\-15; Documented database adapters; pin driver versions\.
- core:fly\-docker: [Fly Dockerfile deployment](https://docs.fly.io/languages-and-frameworks/dockerfile); checked 2026\-11\-15; Container application deployment, regional routing and persistent process configuration\.
- core:fly\-price: [Fly resource pricing](https://docs.fly.io/about/pricing); checked 2026\-11\-15; Shared CPU is not dedicated CPU capacity; regional prices vary\.
- core:fly\-regions: [Fly\.io regions](https://docs.fly.io/reference/regions); checked 2026\-11\-15; Ashburn and Frankfurt only in this profile; current list does not establish India\.
- core:pg: [PostgreSQL introduction](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/intro-whatis.html); checked 2026\-11\-13; Relational engine, transactional integrity
- core:supabase\-price: [Supabase Pro pricing](https://supabase.com/pricing); checked 2026\-11\-15; Single Pro project bundle and usage allowances; not a HIPAA\-eligible contracted plan\.
- core:supabase\-regions: [Supabase specific project regions](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/regions); checked 2026\-11\-15; Pin specific Mumbai, Frankfurt or US East project region; APAC general region is not India\.
- services:aws\-logs: [CloudWatch Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/WhatIsCloudWatchLogs.html); checked 2026\-11\-13; Regional logging configuration required\.
- services:ci: [GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/about-github-actions/understanding-github-actions); checked 2026\-11\-13; Build only source/synthetic tests; no production data exports\.
- services:fly\-price: [Fly resource pricing](https://docs.fly.io/about/pricing); checked 2026\-11\-15; Shared CPU is not dedicated CPU capacity; regional prices vary\.
- services:gcp\-logs: [Regional Cloud Logging](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/regionalized-logs); checked 2026\-11\-13; Regional log buckets and routing configuration\.
- services:pg\-rls: [PostgreSQL row security](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-rowsecurity.html); checked 2026\-11\-13; Policies/forced RLS with owner/BYPASSRLS caveats\.
- services:pg\-tx: [PostgreSQL transactions](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/tutorial-transactions.html); checked 2026\-11\-13; Atomic application/outbox writes; outbox/worker protocol remains custom\.
- services:stripe: [Stripe Checkout](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout); checked 2026\-11\-13; Hosted checkout; merchant eligibility and integration required\.
- services:stripe\-dpa: [Stripe DPA](https://stripe.com/legal/dpa); checked 2026\-11\-13; Processor contract and transfer\-review starting point, not executed agreement\.
- services:stripe\-pricing: [Stripe pricing](https://stripe.com/pricing); checked 2026\-11\-13; Country/payment\-specific pricing; model fees below are explicitly assumed envelopes, not this page quoted as USD tariff\.
- services:supabase\-compute: [Supabase compute pricing](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/manage-your-usage/compute); checked 2026\-11\-15; Hourly instance billing and one USD 10 compute credit per organization\.
- services:supabase\-price: [Supabase Pro pricing](https://supabase.com/pricing); checked 2026\-11\-15; Single Pro project bundle and usage allowances; not a HIPAA\-eligible contracted plan\.
- services:supabase\-sms\-hook: [Supabase Send SMS hook](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-hooks/send-sms-hook); checked 2026\-11\-15; Custom hook can call a regional provider; MSG91 adapter must be implemented and verified\.
- services:supabase\-storage: [Supabase uploads](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/storage/uploads/standard-uploads); checked 2026\-11\-15; Direct signed upload path avoids sending media through function body limits; resumable uploads for larger files\.
- services:telemetry: [OpenTelemetry Collector](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/collector/); checked 2026\-11\-13; Collection/redaction/export; backend retention must be configured\.
- services:vercel\-logs: [Vercel runtime logs](https://vercel.com/docs/observability/runtime-logs); checked 2026\-11\-15; Native logs are not an unlimited regional archive; redact and review routing/retention\.
- services:ws: [ws](https://github.com/websockets/ws); checked 2026\-11\-13; Node WebSocket server; auth, retries, shared state and deployment required\.
- services:yjs: [Yjs](https://docs.yjs.dev/); checked 2026\-11\-13; CRDT model separate from transport/persistence\.

## Limits and acceptance

- Exploratory analysis only. The original recommendation and original requirements are unchanged.
- Priority stability counts a finite one-at-a-time sweep; it is not a probability, confidence score or exhaustive sensitivity analysis.
- The tradeoff front covers all complete candidates in this finite reviewed catalog, minimizing cost upper bound and operated components while maximizing the ORIGINAL-priority heuristic score. It does not establish real-world optimality or measured architecture quality.
- Functional experiments try eligible single/pair edits only: phone login to email/password, payments off, offline support off, full-text search off, or unsupported ML off. They are changed projects, never solutions satisfying the original brief.
- Within Decision Lab functional experiments, compliance, infrastructure/residency/provider, tenant isolation, availability, budget, team and timeline are never relaxed. A usable hypothetical result is not legal, security or production approval.
- No user assertion authenticates vendor/tenant evidence. Missing contracts, capacity calibration and independent review remain unresolved.
- engine_evaluations counts top-level scenario trials; the baseline recommendation may additionally evaluate one separately labeled budget proposal. Budget proposals are outside the functional-experiment sweep and never change the baseline brief.
- The generated ADR is Proposed; no stakeholder acceptance, implementation or deployment is inferred.

Acceptance, independent review, vendor eligibility, implementation and deployment remain owner tasks. No acceptance is recorded.

baseline.summary: PROVISIONAL STACK — unresolved critical constraints require review before production. modular_monolith recommendation selected from 270 complete compatible plans; month-12 infrastructure planning band USD 366.9–614.06/month.

warnings.message: This paid managed tier is a planning proposal, not validated capacity or an availability SLA. Validate pool limits, concurrent clients, CPU/memory, backup restore and the requested p95/availability before deployment; no automatic HA replicas are assumed.
99.9% is a target, not a product guarantee. The cost model provisions redundancy assumptions; service terms, failover and workload behavior still require verification.

The output proposes technical control designs only. It does not certify compliance, establish legal applicability, execute contracts, or replace an audit. Implement controls and obtain scope-specific review.
Social provider selection and privacy/transfer terms need explicit review; Keycloak is only the local broker.
No measured evidence establishes the 100 ms p95 target; load-test the complete client/network/data path.

Planning bands combine published reference rates and explicitly authored allowances; they are not regional provider quotes or measured workload capacity. Validate sizing, merchant/SMS eligibility, storage, requests and current tariffs before purchase.

limitations: Exploratory analysis only. The original recommendation and original requirements are unchanged.
Priority stability counts a finite one-at-a-time sweep; it is not a probability, confidence score or exhaustive sensitivity analysis.

The tradeoff front covers all complete candidates in this finite reviewed catalog, minimizing cost upper bound and operated components while maximizing the ORIGINAL-priority heuristic score. It does not establish real-world optimality or measured architecture quality.

Functional experiments try eligible single/pair edits only: phone login to email/password, payments off, offline support off, full-text search off, or unsupported ML off. They are changed projects, never solutions satisfying the original brief.

Within Decision Lab functional experiments, compliance, infrastructure/residency/provider, tenant isolation, availability, budget, team and timeline are never relaxed. A usable hypothetical result is not legal, security or production approval.
No user assertion authenticates vendor/tenant evidence. Missing contracts, capacity calibration and independent review remain unresolved.

engine_evaluations counts top-level scenario trials; the baseline recommendation may additionally evaluate one separately labeled budget proposal. Budget proposals are outside the functional-experiment sweep and never change the baseline brief.
